Proposal · Codex UI · 2026-08-15 · approved and built the same day — the live codex is in scripts/ui/codex.gd; Gallery and Field notes ship as one rail entry each with chips so the rail never scrolls

Crownless Codex Redesign

The codex today is one shape — a stack of pill tabs over a flat scroll — asked to hold twelve different sizes of thing. This page shows what is dense, what is thin, why it feels hard to steer, and a rail‑and‑ledger layout at the game's real 1000×620 panel size, filled with the real 39 monsters, 21 bosses, 28 folk, 420 uniques.

What the shots say
1

Twelve‑fold density spread under one chrome

Every tab is the same tabs‑over‑scroll shape. Monsters is a 6,464 px scroll (17 screens); Rules is 542 px (1.4 screens). The same gesture — open a tab, scroll — has to serve a two‑paragraph page and a forty‑card catalogue.

2

Up to three rows of tabs before content

Gear › Shapes stacks Bestiary/Gear/…, then Shapes/Uniques/…, then seven slot pills: ~150 px of the 620 px panel is navigation, and the first weapon row starts at y≈540. Even the flat tabs give the reader only ~380 px of list.

3

Prose sits in front of the catalogue

Monsters opens on two rule cards (Elites, Temptations — 380 px) before the first monster; Shapes opens on four sentences of budget rules. Reference text and browsable entries share one column, so the entry you came for is below the fold every time.

4

No index, filter, or jump

Forty‑one monster cards in a single scroll with no chapter grouping, no search, no way to land on “the Blightmarsh mobs”. Bosses have a Mechanics button that opens a separate screen and a Back button — a detour, not a detail.

5

Small stalenesses seen on the way

The Gems shelf draws coloured squares although 140 authored gem icons now ship; the Gallery is a 5‑column portrait grid unlike anything else in the book. Neither is structural — both fall out of the layout below.

The proposal — try it

One book, one shape: a rail of sections on the left (always visible, with counts), a filter bar that replaces the tab stacks, a ledger of compact rows, and the detail for whichever row is selected. Reference pages (rules, statuses, co‑op) render as a single readable column with their own mini‑contents. It is drawn at the game's exact 1000×620 panel with the live data and the codex's own sprites; use the rail, type in the search box, click rows, press ↑ ↓. “Today's screen” swaps in the real screenshot of the same section at the same size.

If the rail is too big a step

An incremental version keeps today's top tabs and fixes the four findings inside them:

  • Collapse the tab stacks to one tab row + one filter row. Bestiary/Gear/Gallery sub‑tabs become chips in a filter row (they already behave like filters); the seven slot pills become a select or chips in the same row.
  • Move the prose out. Elites/Temptations, Shape rules, Gem rules, Bag rules join Rules under one Field notes tab; Monsters/Shapes open on their first entry.
  • Rows, not cards, in the heavy shelves, with the card shown on click (a popover, like the inventory's item card) — Monsters/Bosses/Terrains/Curios drop from 3–6k px to under 2k.
  • Chapter chips + a search box on every collection shelf.

This gets ~70% of the benefit and touches only open()'s nav block and the shelf builders' headers. The rail version is the same builders with the nav moved left and a detail pane added.

How it maps onto codex.gd

Structure

  • open(m, tab) keeps its signature and every open_codex("…") call site; the tab id chooses the rail entry and (for gear_shapes_helmet‑style ids) the initial filter.
  • The three _nav rows become one _rail() builder — a VBox of grouped UITheme.tab buttons with a count label — and one _filter_bar() per section.
  • Collections split each existing shelf builder in two: _rows(section) → Array (data only, sortable, filterable) and _detail(entry) (today's card body, verbatim). _build_chunked still streams the rows; the detail is one card, so it builds synchronously.
  • Prose blocks (Monsters header, Shapes header, Gems/Bags/Rules, Status, Co‑op) move unchanged into a _notes(page) builder — same labels, one reading width.
  • Boss detail folds inline (_boss_detail becomes the fold's content); open_codex("bosses", kind) selects the row + opens the fold. BOSS_KINDS and the dev Transform buttons are unchanged.

Small fixes worth doing regardless

  • Gems shelf: draw Art.gem_icon(color, lv) at Lv 1 / 4 / 7 / 10 instead of a colour square — the authored ladder is the whole point of the 140 icons.
  • Chapter grouping in Monsters/Bosses/Terrains even under the current layout — the data already knows the chapter (this page's chips use it).
  • Gallery: 96×120 frames instead of 160 px cells so Heroes fits on one screen (19 tiles → 2 rows).

Also in this change

Gem sockets — fixed. The 140 authored gem icons were cut on a fixed grid from ImageGen sheets that never honoured the grid; every gem now sits within half a pixel of centre, nothing is clipped, and Garnet shows its authored art again (its stat key had moved to hp_flat).
